findings.summary: Both Kimi rows now admit with AdmissionFlag.Unconfined, so the person sees the shared caveat 'unconfined: can read this machine — a shell is always there, and no flag removes it' next to every Kimi row (the C# caveat here and the TS twin at src_vs_code/src/capabilityAdmission.ts:60). For Kimi this is false: the shim refuses every shell command (M-K3, M-K4), and the rows' own notes say so. The real way Kimi reads outside its folder is Grep and Glob (M-K6). Before this change only codex was unconfined, so the sentence was true until now.
findings.fix: Make the unconfined caveat true for every unconfined runtime on both sides. Either drop the shell clause (e.g. 'unconfined: can read this machine — its tools reach outside the folder coai gives it, and no flag removes that'), or let a row give its own reason. Add a C# test and a TS test that pin Kimi's caveat and fail if it names a shell. Also fix the `unconfined` definition in shared/runtime-capabilities.json:11 ('a shell is always there').

findings.summary: The seed's `why` still says which record each runtime's rows cite: the first five cite the 01a0f8c7 run and the vibe rows cite the M-V cells. It says nothing about the new kimi rows, which cite the M-K cells of research/RESULTS_kimi_confinement.md (kimi 2.1.1). The E5.6 anchors name this text (`:19-20`, 'the `why` naming whose cells the rows cite').
findings.fix: Add one sentence to `why`: the kimi rows cite the M-K cells of research/RESULTS_kimi_confinement.md (Windows, kimi 2.1.1, 2026-10-13). Then run the generator again if any generated text comes from `why`.

findings.summary: In S5.6.7 the 'refused' arm is refused because the granted root is not a git repository. That happens before KimiLaunch makes the home, so no junction exists and this arm cannot show the junction-first disposal on refusal that the story's goal asks for (deviation 52 says so too). Also, in no arm does the test assert that the row's own coai-question-* scratch is gone. It only checks the --cwd copy inside that scratch, and in the refused arm it checks nothing about the scratch.
findings.fix: Add or replace the refused arm with a refusal that comes after the home and its junction exist: for example, the fake person's config changed so that KimiLaunch refuses (launch-refused). Check that the recorder stays empty in that arm. Also assert that the row's scratch folder is gone in every arm. Use the parent of the copy, or seam QuestionRowLaunch.MakeScratch into the test's testsToDelete- folder.
